instructions: Put 3 1/4 cups water, the 3/4 cup sugar and the 2 tsp orange blossom water in a medium pot over medium-high heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Once it bubbles, turn the heat to low and leave it there.
Meanwhile, melt the 3 tbsp butter in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the 3/4 cup semolina and stir constantly for 10 to 15 minutes, until it turns golden brown and smells nutty.
Carefully add the toasted semolina to the pot of syrup. Stand back a little, it will spatter.
Turn the heat up to medium-high and stir constantly for 7 to 8 minutes, until it's thick like porridge and there are no lumps.
Spoon it into 4 bowls and dust each with cinnamon, 1 tsp in all. Serve warm.
method_notes: No version online has 20 ratings, so this leads with The Matbakh's Syrian mamouniyeh (5 from 4 votes), which toasts the semolina in butter, then cooks it in sugar syrup; Cup of Yum (5 from 6) does the same with a little more butter. Scaled to 3/4 of the lead for 4 people. Nuts and string cheese are left out to keep it nut-free and egg-free as the list says. The Matbakh says it keeps 2 days in the fridge, but it's best eaten fresh.
